profile.headline: Advisory Software Engineer @ IBM | IBM i
profile.summary:
I am a hard working individual, and a forever student of my craft. I'm goal oriented. I love having a goal to work towards, getting closer each day, little by little. I'm open to trying to new things, and putting myself into unfamiliar roles. I was awarded my Masters of Computer Science from the University of Minnesota in 2021 while also being a full-time software engineer.

I will be forever grateful to all the professors, teachers, and colleagues who have helped me get to where I am today. I love what I do, and do I what I love.

Contact me and we can talk programming, school, or just about anything technology related.

positions.title: Advisory Software Engineer
positions.description: I work on the Integrated File Systems & Servers Team for the IBM i O/S. I help create new capabilities for future enhancements to the OS and provide product support for older releases. I lead work efforts on my team from requirements gathering until final testing. I advise others outside of my team on efforts in my area of expertise.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
I work on the Integrated File Systems & Servers Team for the IBM i O/S. I help create new capabilities for future enhancements to the OS and provide product support for older releases.
I work primarily in C++ and Java.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Developed new capabilities for hardware, fixed bugs in current system, developed tools to automate repetitive tasks, and wrote tests to verify changes implemented. I worked with Ada, proprietary testing software, Python, and C# with COM (OLE Automation).

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description: Assisting a Professor in his dissertation by developing an algorithm and program to successfully interpret an ancient Hmong dialect and translate it into a more readable dialect.

positions.title: Supplemental Instructor
positions.description: Answer questions students have in conjunction with helping an assigned Professor. Help students with understanding the basic concepts of programming.

positions.title: RoboAcademy Intern
positions.description:
Developing simulation software to replicate the moon's surface. The purpose is to send a LMR (Lunar Micro Rover) weighing less then 10kg to the moon with other payloads. 

The proposed objective is that the LMR will take pictures of the moon's surface that will generate a 3D virtual moon in the simulation which researchers can then document more accurately.

The simulation software is designed with the ability to send batch commands to the LMR. Once on the moon the path can be simulated first and then sent to the LMR hopefully providing a more reliable path.

positions.title: Research Associate
positions.description: I developed an internet model to incorporate into an already existing computer simulation to test NASA advanced concepts with. It was to determine if instead of using ADS-B researchers could instead use the internet and then to model the potential problems that could arise with such an infrastructure.

educations.fieldOfStudy: Applied Mathematics & Computer Science and Game Design & Development

volunteerExperiences.description: Oversaw the Brainz room during school hours. The Brainz room is a room for students who need extra help during class, were absent and didn't get homework done, and a room to just play in. I helped tutor students from 6th - 8th grade ranging in topics from math, global studies, and spelling.

Technovation offers girls around the world the opportunity to learn the skills they need to emerge as tech entrepreneurs and leaders. Every year they invite girls to identify a problem in their community, and then challenge them to solve it.

Girls work in teams to build both a mobile app and a business plan to launch that app, supported by mentors and guided by a curriculum.

Technovation's curriculum takes students through 4 stages of launching a mobile app startup, inspired by the principles of design thinking:

Ideation       - Identify a problem in the community
Technology - Develop a mobile app solution
Entrepreneurship - Build a business plan to launch the app
Pitch - Bring the business to market


I had the wonderful opportunity to be a mentor to 4 teams at St. John the Evangelist. These young woman were motivated, hard working, and silly. It was an absolute blast to get to watch there idea take form, to see them code it and make it a reality, and watch them prepare to pitch it. I believe they will do great things for this world. - 05/17

projects.title: Advanced Software Engineering Project
projects.description: I am working with a team to develop software that will allow professor to communicate with students via social networking platforms. If a professor wants to send out a single message they can send it using e-mai, Facebook, and Twitter.

projects.title: Dream Quarantine
projects.description:
Dream Quarantine is a game being developed for my senior level game design class. 
It is developed in C# using Unity.

publications.title: Proof-of-Concept of a Networked Validation Environment for Distributed Air/Ground NextGen Concepts
publications.publisher: 2013 Aviation Technology, Integration, and Operations (ATIO) Conference · Apr 29, 2013

organizations.name: Stout's Academic Honor Society
organizations.description: I was the chapter President for Stout's Academic Honor Society, which is an organization dedicated to high academic achieving students and furthering their potential both academically and professionally.
